status: Closed — sealed attribution transaction and concurrency regressions verified 2026-09-03
finding: Governed commit admission is path-scoped but not yet proven content-attributed across every success path. Broker apply code also needs proof that shared-delivery admission happens before commit-tree/update-ref effects. A same-path staged blob swap or late admission rejection could produce a successful commit whose actual tree does not match the admitted bundle.
expectedBehavior: Every governed commit must seal path, mode, blob/content digest, and provenance before any ref mutation; temporary-index assembly must consume that sealed bundle; rejected admission must leave HEAD unchanged; receipts must be derived from the actual committed tree. Multiple captains may prepare sealed bundles in parallel, but the branch ref update must be broker-managed through queue/wait or CAS retry. Override leases are exceptional repair authority, not the normal answer to daily multi-captain commits.
evidenceOrRepro: Captain source review on 2026-07-31 found current atm git commit already uses task-scoped temporary index execution from TASK-GIT-0028, so the older no-isolation claim is stale. Remaining evidence-backed concern is success-path content attribution and broker apply/admission ordering around packages/cli/src/commands/git-governance/** and packages/cli/src/commands/broker/batch-execute-actions.ts.
followUp: Resolved by the sealed task-scoped candidate-index transaction: path, mode, blob, and provenance are sealed before assembly; candidate and committed trees are both compared against that seal; and the concurrency/override-free fixtures cover CAS and rejected attribution paths. Revalidated 2026-09-03 with `sealed-commit-attribution.test.ts`, `commit-attribution-sealed-transaction.test.ts`, and `commit-attribution-concurrency-gates.test.ts`. The latter's no-op callback is now correctly asserted as a post-commit-attribution failure rather than a successful transaction.
